questions.q: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.why: Honest starts with a silent h, so the first sound is a vowel sound (o). Use an.

questions.q: ___ Ganga is a holy river.
questions.why: Rivers take the. There is only one Ganga, and we all know which one.

questions.q: How ___ water is in the glass?
questions.why: Water can't be counted, so use much. Many is for things you can count.

questions.q: She has ___ friends, so she often feels lonely.
questions.why: Few means hardly any, which fits feeling lonely. A few means some.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.why: We don't use an article before names of sports.

questions.q: What is a group of sheep called?
questions.why: A flock of sheep. A herd is for cows, a swarm for bees, a pack for wolves.

questions.q: What is the plural of baby?
questions.why: A word that ends in a consonant plus y changes y to ies: babies.

questions.q: Honesty is which kind of noun?
questions.why: Honesty is a quality you can't touch, so it is an abstract noun.

questions.q: This pen belongs to me. It is ___.
questions.why: When no noun follows, use mine. (Before a noun, use my: my pen.)

questions.q: Riya and ___ went to the market.
questions.why: I is the subject word, and it goes last: Riya and I.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym of brave?
questions.why: Bold means about the same as brave. Cowardly is the opposite.

questions.q: What is the antonym of ancient?
questions.why: Ancient means very old, and its opposite is modern.

questions.q: What is the antonym of visible?
questions.why: Visible takes the prefix in-: invisible.

questions.q: Which word means the same as begin?
questions.why: Begin and start are synonyms.

questions.q: What is the antonym of victory?
questions.why: Victory means winning, and its opposite is defeat. The other three are synonyms.

questions.q: Ravi is ___ than Amit.
questions.why: We are comparing two people and the sentence has than, so use the comparative: taller.

questions.q: What is the superlative of good?
questions.why: Good is irregular: good, better, best.

questions.q: In "She has three pens", the word "three" is an adjective of ___.
questions.why: Three tells how many, so it is an adjective of number.

questions.q: What is the comparative of beautiful?
questions.why: Long words use more: more beautiful. Most beautiful is the superlative.

questions.q: Mount Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
questions.why: It is the top of all mountains, so use the superlative with the: the highest.

questions.q: The class starts ___ 8 o'clock.
questions.why: Use at for exact clock times.

questions.q: My birthday is ___ 12 March.
questions.why: Use on for dates and days. (In is for months and years.)

questions.q: I have lived here ___ 2019.
questions.why: Since goes with a starting point (2019). For goes with a length of time (for six years).

questions.q: Share the sweets ___ the four children.
questions.why: Among is for more than two. Between is for two.

questions.q: She is afraid ___ the dark.
questions.why: Afraid goes with of: afraid of.

questions.q: "She is singing a song." Which tense is this?
questions.why: is + singing (verb with -ing) shows something happening right now: present continuous.

questions.q: "They had left before I arrived." Which tense is this?
questions.why: had + the third form (left) shows an action finished before another past action: past perfect.

questions.q: What is the passive voice of "Mohan eats an apple"?
options: An apple was eaten by Mohan.
An apple is eaten by Mohan.
An apple is being eaten by Mohan.
An apple has eaten by Mohan.
questions.why: Simple present passive: is/am/are + the third form. An apple is eaten by Mohan.

questions.q: What is the passive voice of "They will complete the work"?
options: The work will complete by them.
The work is completed by them.
The work will be completed by them.
The work was completed by them.
questions.why: Future passive: will be + the third form. The work will be completed by them.

questions.q: What is the active voice of "The window was broken by the boy"?
options: The boy has broken the window.
The boy is breaking the window.
questions.why: The passive is in the simple past (was broken), so the active is the simple past: The boy broke the window.
